modal:index:AppDeployment.description: Deploys a Modal App from a Python app file by running `modal deploy`, and manages the deployed App. The Modal CLI must be installed on the machine that runs Pulumi (`pip install modal`), because Modal builds Function definitions client side and only the CLI can ship them. The App is redeployed in place whenever the contents of the source directory (or a trigger) change, and stopped on delete. Reports the App's Functions and web endpoint URLs. Importing by App ID restores the outputs but not appFile, so the first update after an import redeploys. See https://modal.com/docs/guide/managing-deployments.

appFile.description: Path to the Python file that defines the Modal App. A relative path resolves against the directory Pulumi runs the program from.

appId.description: The Modal-assigned identifier of the deployed App.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the CLI process, for values the app file reads while it is being built. Treated as secret. The Modal credentials, environment and endpoint are always set from the provider configuration.

environment.description: The Modal environment to deploy into. Changing this forces a new resource. When unset, the provider-level environment or the account's default environment is used.

functions.description: Names of the Functions the deployed App exposes, sorted.

modalCommand.description: The command, with any leading arguments, that starts the Modal CLI, for example ["uv", "run", "modal"]. Defaults to ["modal"].

name.description: The deployed App's name, passed to the CLI as --name. Changing this forces a new resource.

sourceDir.description: Directory whose contents are fingerprinted to decide when to redeploy; .git, __pycache__, .venv, venv and node_modules are skipped. Defaults to the directory of appFile.

sourceHash.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the source directory at the last deploy.

tag.description: Label for this deployment version, passed to the CLI as --tag.

tokenId.description: Modal API token ID. Overrides the provider-level tokenId.

tokenSecret.description: Modal API token secret. Overrides the provider-level tokenSecret.

triggers.description: Values that redeploy the App when any of them changes, for inputs the source fingerprint cannot see.

webUrls.description: Public web endpoint URL of each Function that has one, keyed by Function name.

workingDirectory.description: Directory the Modal CLI runs in. Defaults to the directory of appFile.

modal:index:Environment.description: A Modal environment — a sub-namespace of a workspace that holds Secrets, Volumes, Queues, Dicts, Apps and Images. Environments are workspace-level. Deleting one deletes everything in it. See https://modal.com/docs/guide/environments.

defaultMemberRole.description: Role every workspace member has in this environment unless set individually: `viewer`, `contributor` or `no_access`. Updates in place. Left as is when unset: removing the property does not reset the role, set it to the new value instead. Per-user and service-user role bindings are not modelled yet.

modal:index:Image.description: A Modal Image built from a registry base image plus optional Dockerfile commands, optionally published under a stable name. Changing the base image, commands, environment variables, GPU, registry secret or environment builds a new Image and replaces this one (the old Image is deleted first, because Modal image IDs are content-addressed and a rebuild of an identical definition would otherwise reuse the Image being replaced). An imported Image keeps whatever it was built from, and its environment is detected from where it is published. Modal image IDs are content-addressed, so two Images with the same definition share one ID. Destroying one keeps the image while any environment still publishes a name for it; two unpublished Images with the same definition cannot be told apart, so destroying either deletes the image the other uses. See https://modal.com/docs/guide/images.

baseImage.description: Registry image to start from, for example "python:3.12-slim". Required when creating an Image. Changing this builds a new Image.

dockerfileCommands.description: Dockerfile instructions applied on top of the base image in a single layer, for example "RUN pip install torch". Changing this builds a new Image.

env.description: Environment variables set in the build environment of the Dockerfile commands layer. Changing this builds a new Image.

environment.description: The Modal environment the Image is built and published in. Changing this forces a new resource. When unset, the provider-level environment or the account's default environment is used.

gpu.description: GPU reserved for the build of the Dockerfile commands layer, for example "T4" or "A100:2". Changing this builds a new Image.

imageId.description: The Modal-assigned identifier of the built Image.

name.description: Publishes the built Image under a stable name, "name" or "name:tag" (tag defaults to latest). Changing this republishes the same Image under the new name.

registrySecret.description: Name of a Modal Secret holding credentials for a private registry. Changing this builds a new Image.

modal:index:ServiceUser.description: A Modal service user: a non-human workspace identity with its own API token, for CI/CD and automation. Modal returns the token secret only when the service user is created, so it is kept in state as a secret and cannot be recovered by an import. Modal has no update call, so every input change replaces the service user (and rotates its token). See https://modal.com/docs/guide/service-users.

expiresAt.description: When the service user's token expires, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Unset when it never expires.

expiresInSeconds.description: Expire the service user's token after this many seconds. Unset means it never expires. Changing this forces a new resource.

name.description: The service user's name, unique within the workspace. Changing this forces a new resource.

scoped.description: Restrict the service user to the environments it is granted a role in instead of the whole workspace. Defaults to false. Changing this forces a new resource.

serviceTokenId.description: The ID of the service user's own API token, to use as MODAL_TOKEN_ID.

serviceTokenSecret.description: The service user's API token secret, to use as MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET. Only available when Pulumi created the service user; an imported service user has none.

serviceUserId.description: The Modal-assigned identifier of the service user.

modal:index:Volume.description: A Modal Volume — a persistent, distributed filesystem mountable into Modal Functions and Sandboxes for caching model weights, datasets, or other large files across runs. See https://modal.com/docs/guide/volumes.

environment.description: The Modal environment the volume lives in. Changing this forces a new resource, which deletes the volume's data. When unset, the provider-level environment or the account's default environment is used.

fsVersion.description: Volume filesystem version: "v1" or "v2". Defaults to "v2" (Modal's recommended backend; note that Modal's own SDKs default to "v1"). The effective version is always reported as an output. Changing this forces a new resource and deletes the volume's data: the old volume is deleted before the new one is created because both share a name.

modal:index:WebhookToken.description: A Modal proxy auth token: the key and secret a caller sends in the Modal-Key and Modal-Secret headers to reach a web endpoint that requires proxy authentication. Modal returns the secret only when the token is created, so it is kept in state as a secret and cannot be recovered by an import. The name updates in place; changing scoped replaces the token (and rotates it). Attaching a scoped token to environments is not modelled yet. See https://modal.com/docs/guide/webhook-proxy-auth.

modal:index:WorkspaceSettings.description: The settings of the Modal workspace the API token belongs to: its default environment and image builder version. A workspace has exactly one set of settings, so this is a singleton: declare it at most once per workspace. It is created by applying the settings you set and the import ID is the workspace ID. Modal cannot unset either setting, so removing a setting from the program, or destroying this resource, leaves the workspace as it is.

defaultEnvironment.description: Name of the workspace's default environment, used when a client does not name one. The environment must exist. Unset leaves the workspace default as it is.

imageBuilderVersion.description: Image builder version the workspace builds images with, for example `2024.10`. Unset leaves the workspace version as it is.

tokenId.description: Modal API token ID. Overrides the provider-level tokenId.

tokenSecret.description: Modal API token secret. Overrides the provider-level tokenSecret.

workspaceId.description: The identifier of the workspace the settings belong to. This is also the resource ID.

status.description: The service user's status as reported by Modal.

modal:index:getVolume.description: Look up an existing Modal Volume by name.

environment.description: The Modal environment to look in. Falls back to the provider-level environment, then the account's default environment.

name.description: The object's name.

environment.description: The environment the object was found in: the one that was searched, else the account default environment.

name.description: The Volume's name.

volumeId.description: The Modal-assigned identifier of the Volume.

modal:index:getWebhookToken.description: Look up an existing Modal proxy auth token by name. The secret is never returned.

name.description: The token's name. Fails when more than one token has this name.

createdAt.description: When the token was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp (empty when Modal reports none).

name.description: The token's name.

scoped.description: Whether the token is restricted to the environments it is attached to.

webhookTokenId.description: The Modal-assigned identifier of the token, sent as the Modal-Key header. The secret is never returned.

modal:index:getWorkspace.description: Describe the Modal workspace the provider's token belongs to.

tokenId.description: The ID of the token the provider authenticates with.

workspaceId.description: The identifier of the workspace the token belongs to.

modal:index:getWorkspaceSettings.description: Read the settings of the Modal workspace the provider's token belongs to: its default environment and image builder version.

defaultEnvironment.description: Name of the workspace's default environment.

imageBuilderVersion.description: The image builder version the workspace builds images with.

workspaceId.description: The identifier of the workspace the token belongs to.
